# truenas_vm_power (Resource)

Manages the power state of an existing VM (vm.start / vm.stop / vm.restart) as its own resource, so it can be applied after the VM's truenas_vm_device resources: a new VM then boots with its disks and NICs attached. Leave `running` unset on the truenas_vm. Works in OpenTofu, which has no actions. Destroying this resource leaves the VM in its current state; the truenas_vm's own destroy stops it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A VM whose power state is managed separately from the VM, so it boots only
# once its disk and NIC exist. Leave `running` unset on the truenas_vm.
resource "truenas_vm" "web" {
  name   = "web"
  memory = 2048
  vcpus  = 2
}

resource "truenas_vm_device" "web_disk" {
  vm = truenas_vm.web.id
  attributes = jsonencode({
    dtype = "DISK"
    path  = "/dev/zvol/tank/vms/web"
    type  = "VIRTIO"
  })
}

resource "truenas_vm_device" "web_nic" {
  vm = truenas_vm.web.id
  attributes = jsonencode({
    dtype      = "NIC"
    type       = "VIRTIO"
    nic_attach = "br0"
  })
}

# Applied after both devices: the VM starts with them attached. A change to
# any restart_triggers value (here: the disk device or the VM's memory) while
# running restarts the VM so the guest picks it up. Works in OpenTofu too,
# which has no actions.
resource "truenas_vm_power" "web" {
  vm_id   = truenas_vm.web.id
  running = true
  restart_triggers = {
    disk   = truenas_vm_device.web_disk.attributes
    memory = tostring(truenas_vm.web.memory)
  }
  depends_on = [truenas_vm_device.web_disk, truenas_vm_device.web_nic]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `running` (Boolean) Desired power state: true starts the VM (vm.start), false stops it (vm.stop, graceful with force after the VM's shutdown timeout). Read back from the VM's status, so a VM stopped or started outside Terraform plans its way back.
- `vm_id` (Number) ID of the VM (truenas_vm.<name>.id). Changing it moves the resource to another VM (replacement, no API call for the old VM).

### Optional

- `overcommit` (Boolean) Allow vm.start even if it would overcommit host memory. Default false.
- `restart_triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary strings; when any value changes while running = true, the VM is restarted (vm.restart) so a change the guest only picks up at boot takes effect, for example `{ disk = truenas_vm_device.disk.attributes, memory = tostring(truenas_vm.x.memory) }`. Only compared, never sent to the API.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The VM id as a string.
- `status` (String) VM status as reported by vm.status after the last apply or refresh: RUNNING, STOPPED, SUSPENDED.
